faq.q: Why does a surprise in music give you chills?
faq.a: Your brain keeps predicting what comes next. A thrilling surprise, like a key change or a soaring voice, sets off a burst of emotion and a reward response.
Dopamine is a chemical messenger in the brain linked to reward and pleasure. Brain scans show it is released at the most moving moments in music.
asks: Which brain chemical makes music feel good?

faq.q: Why do the chills come with goosebumps?
faq.a: Strong emotion excites your body's automatic nervous system, which pulls on tiny muscles at the base of your hairs, the same ones that work when you're cold.
asks: Why do my arms tingle when I hear music?

faq.q: Does everyone get chills from music?
faq.a: No. Studies suggest more than half of people do, at least sometimes. It depends on the person and the music.
asks: Is it normal to get chills from music?

faq.q: What kind of music gives chills?
faq.a: Any kind can, from film scores and choirs to rock, Bollywood or K-pop. Big build-ups, sudden changes and a solo voice rising high are common triggers.

facts: A 2011 brain-scan study found dopamine is released at peak emotional moments while people listen to music.
Musical chills are also called frisson, from the French word for shiver.
